description: Audit permissive browser G2P candidates and licenses
notes: Audited candidates: ephone and Piper paths inherit GPL eSpeak-NG; Phonetisaurus.js is MIT but provides no licensed English FST model; Misaki Pyodide is a heavy non-equivalent Python/WASM stack with component-specific licenses; phonemize 2.0.0 is MIT/pure JS and browser-targeted, so it was selected for an empirical parity screen.

description: Adapt the viable candidate to Inflect token input
notes: No candidate was viable to adapt: the only permissive browser-targeted candidate, phonemize 2.0.0, diverges substantially from the upstream eSpeak en-us phonemes before token mapping.

description: Measure corpus phoneme and token parity
notes: Compared MIT phonemize 2.0.0 against upstream VITS frontend fixture using identical Python-normalized strings. Exact phoneme parity was 0/6; character-position agreement was only 4.9%–9.4%, with major vowel/stress/consonant differences. Evidence: fixtures/permissive-g2p-evaluation.json.
